payload.headline: activation_rate_7d fell 22.25% for Microsoft-calendar workspaces after rel_0412 removed the calendar-connect skip option, driving the overall -7.33% decline

cause.does_not_prove: Does not identify which segment or mechanism drove the decline.
cause.text: Overall activation_rate_7d fell from 0.4011 to 0.3717 (-7.33% relative, p=5e-6) between baseline (2026-01-05 to 2026-02-08) and recent (2026-02-09 to 2026-03-01) periods.

cause.does_not_prove: Concentration in one segment does not by itself identify the mechanism or confirm a product cause.
cause.text: The decline is concentrated in calendar_provider=microsoft (0.3937 to 0.3061, -22.25% relative, p=0.0), while google (-0.42%, p=0.84) and none (+8.29%, p=0.28) segments show no significant change.

cause.does_not_prove: Timing correlation alone does not prove causation without a mechanism linking the release to the metric.

evidence.quote: New users connect their calendar before anything else, so the notetaker joins their next meeting automatically. The skip option is removed.

cause.text: rel_0412 ('Onboarding v2: connect calendar first') shipped 2026-02-10, one day into the recent period, at the onset of the decline.

cause.does_not_prove: Does not by itself explain why connected users fail to reach a first meeting; ticket evidence supplies that.
cause.text: In the microsoft segment, calendar_connect_rate_1d rose +60.04% (p approx 0) after rel_0412, but first_meeting_rate_7d fell -14.84% (p approx 0) - the earliest funnel step moving in the same direction as the activation decline, making it the mechanism rather than calendar connection.

cause.does_not_prove: 9 tickets is a lower bound; does not measure how many workspaces silently dropped off without contacting support.

evidence.quote: I just signed up and the setup won't let me past connecting Outlook. It says I need admin approval. Is there a way to skip this for now?
Getting "admin consent required" when I connect Outlook. Our IT team takes a week to approve new apps. Any workaround so I can use the trial meanwhile?

cause.text: 9 distinct Microsoft-calendar workspaces filed tickets between 2026-02-10 and 2026-03-01 describing being blocked at the mandatory calendar-connect step by Microsoft 365 admin-consent requirements, with no skip option available.

payload.cheapest_test: Ship a flag scoped to calendar_provider=microsoft that restores the skip-calendar option (or exempts users hitting Microsoft admin-consent errors) - rel_0412 currently has no flag (flag: null per releases.list_releases) - and watch first_meeting_rate_7d and activation_rate_7d for that segment over the next week before committing to a full rollback.
payload.question: Did 7-day activation change in the last few weeks, and if so why?
payload.recommendation: Roll back or flag-scope rel_0412 to exempt calendar_provider=microsoft workspaces from the mandatory, skip-less calendar-connect-first step until a Microsoft-365-admin-consent-friendly flow ships. Estimated $24,783/week in at-risk ARR from this segment.

ruled_out.does_not_prove: Does not rule out that company_size correlates with calendar_provider mix (larger companies more likely to use Microsoft); it only shows company_size is not the isolating dimension.
ruled_out.text: company_size does not cleanly localize the decline the way calendar_provider does: all four size segments declined to some degree (s11_50 -6.64% p=0.05, s2_10 -7.28% p=0.0022, s51_plus -15.46% p=0.0067, solo -5.96% p=0.064), unlike calendar_provider where google and none segments were flat or positive.

size.method: activation gap x conversion gap (activated vs not) x trials per week in the segment x ARR per paid workspace

unknowns: Whether the true silent drop-off among Microsoft workspaces (beyond the 9 who filed tickets) is large or small.
Whether admin-consent-blocked workspaces eventually connect and activate later, outside the 7-day activation window.
would_change_if: If first_meeting_rate_7d for the microsoft segment recovers on its own as the 1,446 immature recent-cohort workspaces mature, the decline may be a temporary admin-approval lag rather than a permanent block, favoring a wait-and-monitor test over rollback.
If engineering confirms a scoped flag can ship faster than a rollback, set_flag would be preferred over a full release rollback.

findings.claim: The recommendation text is fully grounded in cited data.
findings.evidence: review.check_entry numbers check failed: "'365' in 'Roll back or flag-scope rel_0412 to exempt calendar_provider...Microsoft-365-admin-consent-friendly flow ships' is not in the data." The digit sequence comes from the product name 'Microsoft 365', not from any metric, but code cannot be overridden.
findings.impact: Ledger code checks refuse SHIP whenever an ungrounded number appears in the payload text, regardless of intent; this blocks the packet from reaching the PM as-is.
findings.proof_required: review.check_entry numbers = pass after the edit.
findings.smallest_action: Reword the recommendation to avoid a bare numeral, e.g. 'until an admin-consent-friendly Microsoft calendar flow ships,' then re-run review.check_entry.
